nodes.label: Driving a motor vehicle in Alaska gives implied consent to a breath test measuring alcohol concentration.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After a lawful arrest for driving under the influence, an officer may require a breath sample for alcohol testing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: An officer may require blood or urine testing for alcohol or controlled substances after a crash causing someone else's death or serious physical injury.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: Depending on prior offenses, refusing chemical testing after lawful arrest can be a misdemeanor or a felony.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: The handbook describes driving-under-the-influence and refusal charges as separate charges that a court may handle separately.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: A driver who refuses chemical testing has no limited work-purpose driving privilege during revocation.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After a crash or moving violation, an officer with probable cause of alcohol impairment may require a preliminary roadside breath sample.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Refusal of a preliminary breath test is an infraction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook identifies jail, fines, impoundment, legal expenses, insurance costs and loss of driving privileges as possible consequences of driving under the influence.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The manual assigns ten driving-record points to a driving-under-the-influence offense and says the offense remains on the record permanently.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A designated driver, taxi or public transportation is an alternative to driving after drinking.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Using a false or fraudulent driver license to obtain alcohol can cause a sixty-day revocation for a first offense and a one-year revocation for later offenses.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Alaska prohibits alcohol consumption by people younger than twenty-one, according to the manual.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A person under twenty-one may be arrested or cited for operating a motor vehicle, aircraft or watercraft after consuming any amount of alcohol.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For a driver under twenty-one, refusal of a breath test or a test showing any alcohol triggers DMV revocation of a license, driving privilege or eligibility to obtain a license.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The under-twenty-one administrative revocation can proceed even if the criminal citation is dismissed or the person is found not guilty.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For under-twenty-one alcohol operation or refusal, the first administrative revocation lasts thirty days.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For under-twenty-one alcohol operation or refusal, one previous revocation increases the administrative period to sixty days.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For under-twenty-one alcohol operation or refusal, two previous revocations increase the administrative period to ninety days.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For under-twenty-one alcohol operation or refusal, at least three previous revocations increase the administrative period to one year.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A minor's alcohol-operation or chemical-test-refusal conviction is an infraction for which the court orders community service, a fine of up to one thousand dollars, or both.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The manual identifies a breath or blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight or higher as creating a legal presumption of driving under the influence.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After a driving-under-the-influence arrest, refusing breath testing or producing a result of zero point zero eight or higher triggers administrative revocation.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The administrative action for driving under the influence or refusal may proceed despite dismissal of the criminal charge or a not-guilty verdict.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The first administrative revocation for driving under the influence or refusal lasts ninety days.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: One prior driving-under-the-influence or refusal conviction increases the administrative revocation to one year.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Two prior driving-under-the-influence or refusal convictions increase the administrative revocation to three years.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: At least three prior driving-under-the-influence or refusal convictions increase the administrative revocation to five years.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Alaska or out-of-state convictions for driving while intoxicated, driving under the influence or refusal from the preceding fifteen years may determine the revocation period.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: DMV civil proceedings and court proceedings are separate matters that must each be addressed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: During revocation or disqualification, the person may not drive the affected vehicle class or obtain or apply for a license in Alaska or another state.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A person may contest administrative revocation or disqualification by requesting an administrative hearing in writing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The hearing request may use a personal letter or the DMV administrative-hearing form.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A hearing must normally be requested within seven days of the notice's Date Issued, with a statutory late-hearing exception for physical incapacity.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A granted hearing request produces paperwork explaining the hearing laws, procedures and issues.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A timely hearing applicant with a valid driver license receives a temporary license permitting driving until the hearing unless a court has revoked the privilege.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Judgment is the first ability affected by drinking alcohol, according to the manual.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Alcohol depresses normal functioning, slowing reflexes and reducing alertness, vision and judgment.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Each additional drink increases crash risk for someone who drives afterward.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The manual says alcohol-involved crashes among young people occur at lower average blood alcohol levels than among middle-aged or older drivers.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The amount of alcohol entering the body matters more than whether it comes from beer, wine or spirits.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The manual equates the alcohol in twelve ounces of beer, one and one-half ounces of eighty-proof spirits, and four ounces of wine.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Physical condition, emotions, other drugs and food in the stomach can change how alcohol affects the same person at different times.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Coffee, fresh air, food or a cold shower may increase wakefulness but do not sober a person; alcohol elimination requires time.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The liver processes alcohol, and the body eliminates it through the lungs and kidneys.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Combining alcohol with other drugs can be more dangerous for health and road safety than either substance alone.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Because alcohol's effects depend on many factors, it is difficult to judge how much a person can drink before driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The manual gives an average estimate of one hour per drink and about four hours for four drinks, while explicitly recommending that a person who has been drinking should not drive.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A conviction for driving under the influence or refusal requires an ignition interlock on any vehicle the convicted person operates.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After a first driving-under-the-influence or refusal conviction, ignition-interlock installation is required for at least six months.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The ignition-interlock table lists twelve months after a second conviction and eighteen months after a third conviction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The ignition-interlock table lists twenty-four months after a fourth conviction and thirty months after a fifth conviction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The driver is responsible for ignition-interlock installation and maintenance costs.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reinstating driving privileges requires proof of ignition-interlock installation and proof of future financial responsibility.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Alcohol reaches the bloodstream from the stomach and interferes with brain function, reactions, vision and a driver's sense of responsibility.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Alcohol may create false confidence even as it impairs judgment, hearing, speech and balance.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook's impairment chart associates zero point zero two percent with changes in judgment and inhibitions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The impairment chart associates zero point zero six percent with effects on reaction and coordination, and zero point zero eight percent with serious deterioration in driving performance.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The impairment chart associates zero point one zero percent with effects on vision, speech and balance, and zero point one six percent with effects on walking and standing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The impairment chart associates zero point four zero percent with unconsciousness, possible coma and danger of death.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Ask the prescribing doctor about medicine side effects that could affect driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Nonprescription cold and allergy medicines can contain substances that impair driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Excessive doses of stimulants, diet pills, tranquilizers or sedatives can make driving unsafe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not drive after taking illegal drugs; their strength and purity may be unknown.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Alaska prohibits driving under the influence of controlled substances, including narcotic and nonnarcotic medicines rather than only illegal drugs.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The manual applies the same driving-under-the-influence penalties to controlled substances as to alcohol.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Prescribed drugs may cause drowsiness or reduce alertness, and combining drugs with alcohol can increase their effects and be fatal.
